amendment_rule: Any change to questions, budgets, contestants or thresholds after inspecting results requires a new evaluation with a new declaration file; the original declaration and results are retained unmodified.
instructions: Identical system prompt for every contestant: answer the question for the stated repository and revision; cite every claim as {path, start_line, end_line, revision}; if the evidence is absent or the request is ambiguous, say so instead of guessing.

contestants.name: graph_tools
contestants.description: LLM with tools wrapping rw.repo RepoQuery (resolve, symbols, dependencies, dependents, changes_between, history) and investigate, over the indexed graph of the same clone.

contestants.name: plaintext_direct
contestants.description: Single call with the relevant source files at the requested revision(s) plus `git log` for them as prompt text; if the prompt plus completion would exceed the per-task token budget, record a CONTEXT_LIMIT failure (scored incorrect, zero evidence) without truncating.

contestants.name: plaintext_search
contestants.description: LLM with grep, read_file(path, revision, start, end), git_log(path?, rev_range?), git_show(rev, path?) and list_tags tools over the same clone; same bounded outputs.

budget.pacing: wait so that no rolling 60 s window exceeds 8000 tokens; wait time is excluded from latency but recorded
budget.exceeding_budget: the task stops and is scored on what was answered so far; recorded as budget_exhausted

pairing: every contestant runs every question in each repeat; order of contestants randomised per question with a recorded seed

scoring.answer_accuracy: final answer judged correct against expected_answer (required facts present, no contradicting claim, correct revision); ambiguous: correct iff it asks or lists candidates; missing_evidence: correct iff it reports absence. Scored separately from evidence.
scoring.evidence_recall: fraction of expected_citations overlapped (same path and revision, line spans intersect) by a returned citation
scoring.evidence_precision: fraction of returned citations that overlap some expected citation
scoring.citation_validity: fraction of returned citations whose revision resolves in the requested repo (git rev-parse) and whose path exists at that revision with end_line <= file length
scoring.wrong_revision: count of answers whose claims or citations refer to a revision other than the requested/compare revision

primary_metric: grounded_answer_accuracy = answer correct AND evidence_recall > 0 (missing_evidence questions: answer correct and no fabricated citation)
baseline_for_comparison: the stronger of plaintext_direct and plaintext_search by grounded_answer_accuracy, per repository and overall

PASS_if_any: graph_tools grounded_answer_accuracy >= baseline + 15 percentage points with mean tokens per task within +/-20% of the baseline
graph_tools mean tokens per task <= 70% of the baseline with grounded_answer_accuracy and evidence_recall each not lower than the baseline by more than 5 percentage points
threshold.FAIL: neither PASS condition holds and the run is complete
threshold.INCONCLUSIVE: any repeat missing, more than 10% of tasks failed for infrastructure reasons (API errors, not context-limit or budget), or the two repeats disagree on the verdict
threshold.applies_to: overall (both repositories pooled); per-repository verdicts are reported but the claim requires the overall PASS
threshold.tokens_include: prompt + completion tokens of all calls in the task; graph_tools additionally reports indexing cost (E1/E3 records) amortised and un-amortised

cost_model.note: declared assumption for gpt-oss-120b; free tier is actually $0

indexing_cost_source: artifacts/repo_onboarding and E3 scale records (wall seconds, peak memory, tokens if any) for each repo at the evaluated revisions
